correctness.rationale: The sign of a cycle on all selected simplex vertices is (-1)^(m-b) for m selected arrows in b complete arrow orbits; multiplying by the simplicial Euler sign yields (-1)^(b-1), so the orbit counts calculate exact Lefschetz numbers (100,2,0,1,0). Independently the 12,820-face signed simplex-trace code gives the same results for all 24 permutations, with f-vector matching the published table. Scoville Theorem 20 gives rational reduced homology only in degree 4 with rank 99; removing the H0 trace 1 obtains (99,1,-1,0,-1). S4 character-table inner products give nonnegative integer multiplicities (4,13,8,12,4), dimension sum 99. Independent mod-two boundary ranks corroborate the homology premise without being used to claim integral torsion-freeness.

value.rationale: The non-pure tetrahedron is a motivated first three-dimensional test case in the recently published homotopy classification of Morse-matching spaces. Its complete natural S4 homology representation, four invariant classes, four alternating classes, and all Specht multiplicities refine an existing rank-only result and distinguish equivariant information relevant to comparisons with the pure/boundary constructions. The finite invariant is canonical for this complex and non-implied by a nonequivariant wedge decomposition.
